project.description_en: At the end of the theme, the child wears an animal mask, moves like the animal, names it, says what it eats and recites a short animal rhyme in English or in French.

activities.goal_en: Recite a short animal poem with gestures.
activities.prompt_en: Listen and do like the little goat.
steps_en: Say the poem once with gestures.
Say it line by line; the child repeats.
Say it together with the actions.
Ask: what does the goat eat?
source_refs: Nursery One, table 15 (Poetry and Rhymes: Poems), p. 40; theme 6: Animals (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.story_en:
Little goat, little goat, with a bell on your coat,
You eat green grass and you jump on a rock,
Meh, meh, little goat, it is time to go home,
To sleep near the house when the night has come.

activities.title_en: c for cat, d for dog
activities.goal_en: Recognise the first sound of simple animal words.
activities.prompt_en: Listen: c-c-cat. What sound does cat begin with?
steps_en: Show the picture of a cat and say the word slowly.
Say the first sound alone: /k/.
Show the letter c.
Do the same with dog and the letter d.
observe_en: Matches cat with c and dog with d.
Finds another word with the same sound.
materials_en: pictures of a cat and a dog
source_refs: Nursery One, table 17 (Reading: Letter-sounds), p. 42; theme 6: Animals (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.goal_en: Write the lowercase letters c and o in the right direction.
activities.prompt_en: The letter c is like a cat’s back: start at the top and go round. The o closes the circle.
steps_en: Trace c in the air, starting at the top.
Trace o, closing the circle.
Trace them in sand.
Write a row of c and a row of o.
observe_en: Goes round in the right direction.
source_refs: Nursery One, table 18 (Writing: Letters and numbers), p. 43; theme 6: Animals (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.goal_en: Recite a short French rhyme about a hen.
activities.prompt_en: Listen to a little French rhyme: “Une poule, deux poussins, trois grains de maïs dans ma main.”
steps_en: Say the rhyme slowly with fingers: 1, 2, 3.
The child repeats each part.
Say it together.
Ask: what is “une poule” in English? (a hen)
observe_en: Says one French word and its meaning.
materials_en: a picture of a hen and chicks
source_refs: Nursery One, table 19 (French: Poésie et comptines), p. 44; theme 6: Animals (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.goal_en: Count the legs of animals and compare.
activities.prompt_en: How many legs has the hen? And the goat?
steps_en: Show pictures of a hen and a goat.
Count the legs of the hen together.
Count the legs of the goat.
Ask: who has more legs?
observe_en: Says which animal has more legs.
Uses the words more and less.
source_refs: Nursery One, table 20 (Mathematics: Counting), p. 45; theme 6: Animals (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

interactive.prompt_en: How many legs has a goat?
interactive.explanation_en: Count the legs of the goat: one, two, three, four. A goat has 4 legs.

activities.goal_en: Sort animals into big and small.
activities.prompt_en: Is the elephant big or small? And the ant?
steps_en: Show pictures of animals.
Hold up each one and ask big or small.
Put the pictures into two groups.
Count each group.
source_refs: Nursery One, table 20 (Mathematics: Classifying elements), p. 45; theme 6: Animals (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.goal_en: See which things float and which sink in water.
activities.prompt_en: Will the stone float or sink? And the plastic duck?
steps_en: Fill a basin with water.
Ask the child to guess: float or sink?
Put the object in the water and watch.
Sort the objects into two groups.
observe_en: Says float or sink after watching.
source_refs: Nursery One, table 22 (Science and Technology: Gravity), p. 47–48; theme 6: Animals (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.goal_en: Show love and empathy for animals.
activities.prompt_en: Animals feel pain like us. We do not beat them, we give them water and we are gentle.
steps_en: Show pictures of children caring for animals and a child hurting an animal.
Ask: which child is kind?
Talk about what animals need (food, water, shelter).
Act: give water to a toy animal gently.
source_refs: Nursery One, table 25 (Character Education: Good behaviour), p. 51; theme 6: Animals (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.goal_en: Report an injury to an adult at once.
activities.prompt_en: If a dog or a cat scratches or bites you, run to an adult and show the wound.
steps_en: Explain that some animals can scratch or bite.
Act: a child is scratched and tells the teacher.
Show how an adult washes the wound with clean water and soap.
Remind: do not touch unknown dogs.
observe_en: Says they will tell an adult.
Shows the wound to the adult in the role play.
Says not to touch unknown animals.
source_refs: Nursery One, table 28 (Health Education and Nutrition: Treatment), p. 54; theme 6: Animals (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.goal_en: Keep the yard clean so that flies and rats do not come.
activities.prompt_en: When food and rubbish stay on the ground, flies and rats come. Let us keep the yard clean.
steps_en: Walk round the yard and find rubbish.
With gloves or a stick, put it in the bin.
Cover the food and the bin.
Wash hands after.
source_refs: Nursery One, table 26 (Environmental Education: The environment), p. 52; theme 6: Animals (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.goal_en: Make an animal mask with paper and decorate it.
activities.prompt_en: Choose an animal. Let us make its mask!
steps_en: Cut a paper plate or card with holes for the eyes (adult).
Draw the animal’s ears and nose.
Colour and stick the ears.
Add a string and wear the mask.
observe_en: Names the animal when wearing it.
source_refs: Nursery One, table 31 (Handwork: Practice sessions), p. 57; theme 6: Animals (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

activities.title_en: Gallop like a horse, hop like a frog
activities.goal_en: Reproduce different animal movements: galloping and hopping.
activities.prompt_en: Gallop like a horse! Now hop like a frog! Now walk slowly like a tortoise.
steps_en: Show galloping: one foot leads, the other follows.
Show hopping on two feet like a frog.
Call out an animal; the children move like it.
Finish slowly like a tortoise.
source_refs: Nursery One, table 32 (Physical Education and Sports: Athletics), p. 58; theme 6: Animals (table 13, p. 37)

editorial.notes: Activity written for Klassia from the Nursery One contents of the English-subsystem nursery curriculum; original texts. To be reviewed by a Nursery One teacher of the English subsystem.

scale.description: Succeeds mostly with a model or help.
Sometimes succeeds alone, sometimes with a reminder.
Succeeds on their own in a familiar situation.

indicators: Sorts animals into big and small.
Recognises the first sound of cat and dog.
Writes the letters c and o with help.
Says what floats and what sinks.

sources: Cameroon Nursery School Curriculum, English Subsystem, MINEDUB, 2018: table 13 (integrated learning themes), p. 37; Nursery One tables, cited and not reproduced.
